LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we need to write in good handwriting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner’s self- discipline is enhanced when the learn is motivated to practise correct letter formation and writing from left

to right.

Values:
Unity: enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers to practise shaping letters correctly.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: is enhanced as learners confidently shape the letters of the alphabet correctly.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Kiswahili Language activities: as learners relate the concept of legibility in handwriting through the correct formation of lower- case letters

of the alphabet.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
